title: On the survival of dark matter spikes: Stellar and compact-object perturbations
comment: 7 pages, 4 figures + appendices
summary: Establishing realistic expectations for the dark matter (DM) distribution near a supermassive black hole (BH) is essential for assessing environmental imprints on gravitational wave (GW) signals. Using the Galactic Center as an observationally constrained case study, we investigate the evolution of DM density spikes under gravitational perturbations from the nuclear stellar and black hole populations surrounding the central BH. We find that scattering of DM particles by the nuclear star cluster depletes the DM distribution at radii $r \sim 10^{-1}~\mathrm{pc}$, far outside the region where the relevant GW signals are produced. At smaller radii, at $r \sim 10^{-3}~\mathrm{pc}$, the closest known stellar perturbers, S2 and S38, induce only negligible changes to the density profile. At still smaller radii, where no stellar perturbers are currently known, we assess the cumulative impact of past EMRIs by modelling successive mergers with stellar-mass BHs of mass $\sim10~\mathrm{M}_\odot$, in numbers consistent with the expected rate over $10~\mathrm{Gyr}$. We find that these events do not erase the central overdensity, reducing the density only to approximately $82 \%$ of its initial value at $r \lesssim 10^{-5}~\mathrm{pc}$. Our results indicate that, at least at the Galactic Center, DM overdensities around the central BH are expected to remain largely intact under stellar perturbations and plausible stellar-BH merger histories.

AI.tldr: Using the Galactic Center as a case study, the paper finds that DM density spikes around a supermassive BH remain largely intact despite stellar perturbations from the nuclear star cluster (depletion at ~0.1 pc), known stellar perturbers S2/S38 (negligible effect at ~10⁻³ pc), and past EMRIs with stellar-mass BHs (density reduced to ~82% at ≲10⁻⁵ pc). DM overdensities survive these gravitational perturbations.
AI.motivation: To establish realistic expectations for DM distribution near a supermassive BH, which is essential for assessing environmental imprints on gravitational wave signals.
AI.method: Investigates the evolution of DM density spikes under gravitational perturbations from the nuclear stellar and BH populations around the central BH, using the Galactic Center as an observationally constrained case study.
AI.result: (1) Nuclear star cluster depletes DM at r ~ 10⁻¹ pc. (2) S2 and S38 induce negligible changes at r ~ 10⁻³ pc. (3) Past EMRIs reduce density to ~82% of initial value at r ≲ 10⁻⁵ pc.
AI.conclusion: At least at the Galactic Center, DM overdensities around the central BH are expected to remain largely intact under stellar perturbations and plausible stellar-BH merger histories.

title: Turbulence in the multi-phase circumgalactic medium: bridging TNG50 and idealized kpc-scale simulations
comment: To be submitted to the Open Journal of Astrophysics, comments welcome
summary: The circumgalactic medium (CGM) is the extended multi-phase gaseous halo surrounding a galaxy. To study how its dynamics are shaped by the interplay of radiative cooling and turbulence, we first turn to the TNG50 cosmological magnetohydrodynamical simulation. We analyze the turbulent properties of the CGM of Milky Way-like galaxies at z=0, using a multi-scale filtering technique. We find that the CGM hosts predominantly subsonic flows with Mach number ~ 0.1 - 0.7 that are roughly balanced between compressive and solenoidal components with b = M_comp / M_tot ~ 0.3 - 0.6. We then use these physically motivated properties of turbulent CGM media to set the initial conditions and driving parameters for idealized, turbulent box simulations. These represent ~ 1 kpc^3 volumes of the CGM, but reach resolutions higher than available in cosmological volumes such as TNG50. To do so, we implement a turbulent driving algorithm into the AREPO code based on random but smoothly time-fluctuating acceleration fields, and then run a suite of turbulent boxes across the parameter space, including a model for metal-line radiative cooling. Using these simulations, we study how turbulence seeds density fluctuations that trigger thermal instability and promotes mixing between hot and cold phases, depending on the relative timescales of cooling and mixing. The abundance and evolution of cold ~10^4 K gas depends strongly on the strength of turbulence and the efficiency of cooling.

AI.tldr: This study analyzes turbulent properties of the circumgalactic medium (CGM) around Milky Way-like galaxies using TNG50 cosmological simulations, finding predominantly subsonic flows (Mach ~0.1-0.7) with balanced compressive and solenoidal components. The authors then use these properties to set up idealized turbulent box simulations with higher resolution, implementing a turbulent driving algorithm in AREPO with metal-line radiative cooling, to study how turbulence seeds density fluctuations, triggers thermal instability, and promotes mixing between hot and cold phases.
AI.motivation: To understand how the dynamics of the circumgalactic medium (CGM) are shaped by the interplay of radiative cooling and turbulence, and to bridge the gap between cosmological-scale simulations and high-resolution idealized studies of turbulent CGM physics.
AI.method: The authors first analyze turbulent properties of the CGM in the TNG50 cosmological magnetohydrodynamical simulation using a multi-scale filtering technique. They then use these physically motivated properties to set initial conditions and driving parameters for higher-resolution idealized turbulent box simulations, implementing a turbulent driving algorithm in AREPO based on random, smoothly time-fluctuating acceleration fields, with a metal-line radiative cooling model.
AI.result: The CGM hosts predominantly subsonic flows with Mach numbers ~0.1-0.7, and the turbulent modes are roughly balanced between compressive and solenoidal components (b = M_comp/M_tot ~ 0.3-0.6). The abundance and evolution of cold ~10^4 K gas in the idealized simulations depend strongly on the strength of turbulence and the efficiency of cooling.
AI.conclusion: Turbulence seeds density fluctuations that trigger thermal instability and promotes mixing between hot and cold phases in the CGM, with the outcome depending on the relative timescales of cooling and mixing. Higher-resolution idealized simulations can capture cold gas dynamics that cosmological volumes like TNG50 cannot resolve.

title: CANUCS/Technicolor Data Release 2: A Catalogue of Galaxy Structural Parameters in up to 29 HST+JWST bands and a Multi-Wavelength Exploration of the Galaxy Size-Mass Relation at $0.6 < z \leq 4$
comment: Submitted to ApJ; 30 pages, 16 figures; comments welcome. Data products available at https://niriss.github.io/data.html
summary: We present James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) results of a morphological study of galaxies in the CAnadian NIRISS Unbiased Cluster (CANUCS) and Technicolor surveys, observed in 19 medium- and broadband NIRCam filters in five CANUCS NIRCam Flanking Fields with rest-frame wavelength coverage between $\sim 0.2 - 3.2μm$. Using GALFIT, we measure the morphological parameters of $\sim$ 4,100 star-forming galaxies at $0.6 < z \leq 4$ with stellar masses of $8.5 < \text{log}(M_*/M_\odot) \leq 11.5$. This enables us to concurrently examine how galaxy size varies as a function of stellar mass, redshift, and rest-frame wavelength to provide a novel parametrization of the galaxy size-wavelength relation. Additionally, we analyze the evolution of the galaxy size-mass relation in the rest-frame optical and NIR with the introduction of wavelength as a free parameter. We report a gradient in the slope of the size-mass relation with respect to rest-frame wavelength with a critical crossover mass at $\sim 10^{9.5} M_\odot$. We propose this characteristic mass as the stellar mass at which galaxies transition between diffuse and compact morphologies. We concurrently present the data release of morphological measurements of the five CANUCS-Technicolor NIRCam Flanking Fields in which we provide structural parameters for $\sim$ 41,000 galaxies in up to 29 JWST+HST filters.

AI.tldr: This paper presents JWST morphological measurements of ~4,100 star-forming galaxies at 0.6<z≤4 using GALFIT across 19 NIRCam filters, examining size-mass and size-wavelength relations with a critical crossover mass at ~10^9.5 M⊙, and releases structural parameters for ~41,000 galaxies in up to 29 JWST+HST filters.
AI.motivation: To understand how galaxy sizes vary as functions of stellar mass, redshift, and rest-frame wavelength, and to provide a novel parametrization of the galaxy size-wavelength relation using high-resolution JWST NIRCam data across a broad wavelength range (0.2–3.2 μm rest-frame).
AI.method: Morphological analysis using GALFIT on ~4,100 star-forming galaxies at 0.6<z≤4 (stellar mass 8.5<log(M*/M⊙)≤11.5) observed in 19 medium- and broadband NIRCam filters from the CANUCS and Technicolor surveys, covering rest-frame wavelengths ~0.2–3.2 μm. The size-wavelength relation is parametrized, and the size-mass relation evolution is analyzed with wavelength as a free parameter. A public data release includes structural parameters for ~41,000 galaxies in up to 29 JWST+HST filters.
AI.result: A gradient in the slope of the size-mass relation is found with respect to rest-frame wavelength, with a critical crossover mass at ~10^9.5 M⊙, proposed as the stellar mass marking the transition between diffuse and compact galaxy morphologies.
AI.conclusion: The discovery of a wavelength-dependent size-mass relation gradient with a characteristic crossover mass at ~10^9.5 M⊙ provides new insights into galaxy structural evolution, and the public data release enables further community studies of galaxy morphology across a wide wavelength range.

title: The host halo masses of AGNs and quasars at $z \sim 3-7$ with TNG-Cluster, FLAMINGO and other cosmological galaxy simulations
comment: Key Figures: 1,2, 5. Submitted to MNRAS (20 pages, 6 Figures)
summary: Most observations and clustering analyses suggest that quasars inhabit a narrow range of dark-matter halo masses ($10^{12-13}$ M$_{\odot}$) across cosmic time ($z\lesssim7$). Recent hydrodynamical simulations in gigaparsec-scale volumes now enable direct comparison of this picture with self-consistent galaxy-formation models. We quantify the relation between AGN bolometric luminosity and host halo mass before Cosmic Noon in TNG300, TNG-Cluster, FLAMINGO L1_m8 and L2p8_m9, and in smaller-volume simulations (Illustris, EAGLE, TNG100, and Simba). For AGNs with $L^{\mathrm{AGN}}_{\mathrm{bol}} \ge 10^{42}$ erg s$^{-1}$, more massive haloes host more luminous AGNs on average, but only up to a certain mass. The median luminosity-halo mass relation is highly non-linear, with large scatter, and flattens (FLAMINGO) or turns over (TNG300+TNG-Cluster) at halo mass, $M_{\mathrm{200,crit}} \gtrsim10^{12}$ M$_{\odot}$, at least at $z<5$-6. This high mass AGN quenching also manifests as a characteristic quasar host halo mass: in TNG300+TNG-Cluster, quasars ($L^{\mathrm{AGN}}_{\mathrm{bol}} \sim10^{45-47}$ erg s$^{-1}$) typically reside in haloes of mass $10^{12-12.5}$ M$_{\odot}$ at $z=3$-6, while FLAMINGO quasars extend to median masses of $\sim10^{12.8}$ M$_{\odot}$ at $z\sim3$-4. All simulations predict substantially larger scatter in AGN luminosity at fixed halo mass than in halo mass at fixed luminosity (up to 3 dex versus $\lesssim1$ dex between the 5th and 95th percentiles), implying weak coupling between halo growth and instantaneous SMBH accretion. Consequently, simulated quasar host masses broadly agree with observational estimates. The most luminous AGNs occupy increasingly rare haloes at earlier epochs but typically do not reside in the most massive haloes at any redshift up to $z\approx7$.

AI.tldr: This study uses multiple large-volume hydrodynamical simulations (TNG300, TNG-Cluster, FLAMINGO, etc.) to quantify the relation between AGN bolometric luminosity and host dark-matter halo mass before Cosmic Noon (z<7). It finds a non-linear, highly scattered relation that flattens or turns over at halo masses above ~10¹² M☉, indicating AGN quenching in massive halos. Quasars typically reside in halos of 10¹²–10¹²·⁵ M☉, consistent with observational estimates, but the large scatter implies weak coupling between halo growth and SMBH accretion.
AI.motivation: Observations suggest quasars inhabit a narrow range of dark-matter halo masses (10¹²⁻¹³ M☉) across cosmic time, but this picture has lacked direct, self-consistent comparison with galaxy-formation models from large-volume hydrodynamical simulations — a gap this study aims to fill.
AI.method: The authors analyze AGN bolometric luminosity versus host halo mass in multiple hydrodynamical simulations: gigaparsec-scale (TNG300, TNG-Cluster, FLAMINGO L1_m8, L2p8_m9) and smaller-volume ones (Illustris, EAGLE, TNG100, Simba), focusing on AGNs with L_bol ≥ 10⁴² erg/s across z=0–7.
AI.result: The median luminosity-halo mass relation is highly non-linear with large scatter, flattening (FLAMINGO) or turning over (TNG300+TNG-Cluster) at M_200,crit ≳ 10¹² M☉ (z<5-6). Quasars (L_bol~10⁴⁵⁻⁴⁷ erg/s) reside in halos of ~10¹²⁻¹²·⁵ M☉ (TNG) to ~10¹²·⁸ M☉ (FLAMINGO). Scatter in luminosity at fixed mass is up to 3 dex, while halo mass at fixed luminosity scatters <1 dex. The most luminous AGNs occupy increasingly rare halos at higher redshifts but not the most massive halos at any z≤7.
AI.conclusion: Simulated quasar host masses broadly agree with observational estimates. The large scatter and weak coupling between halo growth and instantaneous SMBH accretion imply that halo mass is not a primary determinant of AGN luminosity at a given epoch.

title: Dynamo Simulations Confirm Predominantly Toroidal Fields in Near-Core Region of an Intermediate-Mass Star
comment: 6 pages, 6 figures, Letter
summary: Recent asteroseismic analysis of the main-sequence F star KIC 9244992 has revealed evidence for a strong, predominantly toroidal magnetic field in its deep radiative interior. Motivated by this result, we present three-dimensional anelastic magneto-hydrodynamic simulations of a rotating 2 solar mass main-sequence star to investigate whether such internal magnetic field strengths and geometries naturally arise in global stellar dynamo simulations for stars within a similar mass range. These simulations self-consistently generate magnetic fields with azimuthal components that dominate over radial components by factors of several near the peak of the Brunt-Vaisala frequency left behind as the core recedes. Moreover, these field strengths arise despite near-uniform, spherically-averaged, rotation from the near-core region to the surface. When the Reynolds number is greater than 100 and the appropriate Rossby number is used, the resulting field strengths and geometrical properties are consistent with those inferred asteroseismically for KIC 9244992. These results indicate that a dominant toroidal field in the near-core region is a generic field configuration in core-convecting stars and should be considered in future asteroseismic inferences.

AI.tldr: Three-dimensional MHD simulations of a rotating 2 solar mass star show that strong, dominantly toroidal magnetic fields naturally arise in the near-core region, consistent with asteroseismic inferences for KIC 9244992, suggesting such fields are generic in core-convecting stars.
AI.motivation: To investigate whether the strong, predominantly toroidal magnetic field inferred asteroseismically in the deep radiative interior of the F star KIC 9244992 can naturally arise in global stellar dynamo simulations for stars of similar mass.
AI.method: Three-dimensional anelastic magneto-hydrodynamic simulations of a rotating 2 solar mass main-sequence star, varying Reynolds and Rossby numbers.
AI.result: The simulations self-consistently generate magnetic fields with azimuthal components dominating over radial components near the peak of the Brunt-Väisälä frequency. For Re > 100 and appropriate Ro, field strengths and geometry match asteroseismic inferences for KIC 9244992.
AI.conclusion: A dominant toroidal field in the near-core region is a generic field configuration in core-convecting stars and should be considered in future asteroseismic inferences.

title: Reconstructing the orbits of Milky Way dwarf galaxies: An LMC perspective
comment: 26 pages, 7 figures, 5 tables, 4 appendices. Submitted to A&A
summary: The orbital histories of the dwarf satellites of the Milky Way (MW) are key to understanding their evolution and placing their present-day properties in a dynamical context. We present the results of the orbit integration of 72 dwarfs in the vicinity of the MW, based on accurate 6D phase-space coordinates from the literature and a suite of six realistic, time-evolving gravitational potentials that account for the mutual interaction of the MW and the Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC). We provide the largest catalogue of orbital parameters for MW dwarfs to date, in terms of both galaxy sample size and range of potentials explored. We also assess the binding status of the dwarfs and estimate their infall times, finding that the majority of them have spent the last 5 Gyr within the MW virial radius. From the reconstructed orbits, we identify ten likely LMC satellites, several of which have experienced very close passages within the LMC stellar disc. For the Small Magellanic Cloud (SMC), we find that its most recent pericentre about the LMC ($\sim$8 kpc, $\sim$170 Myr ago) is consistent with predictions from the direct collision scenario proposed to explain the LMC's offset and tilted bar. We also note a broad temporal coincidence between previous SMC pericentres and star formation rate peaks reported in both Magellanic Clouds, suggesting a causal connection. Finally, we identify Grus II and Tucana IV as possible MW satellites recently captured by the LMC, based on their pronounced orbital deflections and velocities relative to the LMC.

AI.tldr: This paper integrates orbits of 72 Milky Way dwarf satellites using realistic time-evolving potentials that include the MW-LMC interaction, providing the largest orbital catalogue to date, identifying ten LMC satellites, linking SMC-LMC pericenters to star formation, and finding two possible MW satellites recently captured by the LMC.
AI.motivation: Understanding the orbital histories of MW dwarf satellites is crucial for interpreting their present-day properties in a dynamical context, yet previous studies lacked both sample size and realistic treatment of the LMC's gravitational influence.
AI.method: The authors performed orbit integration for 72 dwarf galaxies using 6D phase-space coordinates from the literature across six realistic, time-evolving gravitational potentials that incorporate mutual interactions between the MW and LMC. They derived orbital parameters, assessed binding status, estimated infall times, and identified likely LMC satellites and captured MW dwarfs.
AI.result: The catalogue is the largest to date; most dwarfs spent the last 5 Gyr within the MW virial radius; ten likely LMC satellites were identified; SMC's recent LMC pericenter (~8 kpc, ~170 Myr ago) aligns with the direct collision scenario; temporal coincidence between SMC pericenters and star formation peaks was found; Grus II and Tucana IV are possible recently captured satellites.
AI.conclusion: The time-evolving MW+LMC gravitational framework reveals critical dynamical interactions, including LMC satellite populations, SMC pericenter-driven star formation, and satellite capture events, underscoring the need for realistic multi-body potentials in dwarf galaxy evolution studies.

title: Source Surface Height Optimisation for Improved Solar Wind Velocity Forecasting Across Solar Cycles 23, 24 and 25
comment: Accepted for publication in Astrophysical Journal
summary: The potential field source surface (PFSS) model is a cornerstone of many state-of-the-art space weather forecasting frameworks. It includes a single physical free parameter, the source surface (SS) height. Traditionally, a fixed SS height of 2.5 solar radii has been adopted in most studies. However, several studies have investigated the SS height in the PFSS model using various datasets and temporal intervals. Earlier efforts primarily aimed to improve estimates of the heliospheric open magnetic flux. Our recent study Kumar et al. (2025), showed that optimising the SS height substantially improves the performance of the Wang Sheeley Arge (WSA) solar wind speed prediction model at L1. That analysis employed two types of GONG synoptic magnetic field maps, namely standard (STD) and zero-point-corrected (ZPC) maps, over selected periods of solar cycles (SCs) 24 and 25. In this study, we perform a comprehensive investigation of SCs 23 to 25 using synoptic magnetic field maps derived from ground-based (GONG) and space-based (SDO/HMI) observatories. Our results demonstrate that optimising the SS height in the PFSS model significantly improves the WSA model performance compared to the commonly adopted fixed SS height. We find that during solar minimum, higher SS heights (less than or equal to 2.5 solar radii) yield better solar wind speed predictions at L1, whereas during active phases the opposite trend is observed. Although the absolute optimised SS height varies across SCs, the overall distribution pattern remains similar. These finding suggests a relationship between SS height and SC phase over long time scales. Overall, the SS height optimisation enhances the background solar wind speed prediction models in the heliosphere.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates optimizing the source surface (SS) height parameter in the PFSS model across solar cycles 23-25 using GONG and SDO/HMI magnetograms, finding that dynamic SS height optimization (higher during solar minima, lower during active phases) significantly improves WSA solar wind speed predictions at L1 compared to the traditional fixed 2.5 solar radii height.
AI.motivation: To determine whether optimizing the PFSS model's source surface height, rather than using a fixed 2.5 solar radii value, can improve solar wind speed predictions across multiple solar cycles (23-25) using both ground-based (GONG) and space-based (SDO/HMI) observations.
AI.method: The study uses synoptic magnetic field maps from GONG (STD and ZPC) and SDO/HMI observatories over solar cycles 23-25. The SS height in the PFSS model is optimized and evaluated within the WSA solar wind speed prediction framework, comparing performance against the traditional fixed SS height of 2.5 solar radii across different solar cycle phases.
AI.result: Optimizing SS height significantly improves WSA model performance. Higher SS heights (≤2.5 solar radii) perform better during solar minimum, while lower SS heights perform better during active phases. Although the absolute optimized SS height varies across cycles, the phase-dependent pattern remains consistent.
AI.conclusion: SS height optimization enhances background solar wind speed predictions in the heliosphere, and a relationship exists between SS height and solar cycle phase over long time scales, suggesting the need for phase-dependent tuning rather than a fixed parameter.

title: A novel data-driven approach to extract stellar population properties from galaxy spectra using absorption indices
comment: 20 pages, including 10 figures and 1 table. Submitted to MNRAS
summary: In an era of highly complex machine learning methods that often are informative but not straightforward to interpret, Principal Component Analysis (PCA) offers a simple, easily interpretable approach. With no fitting parameters, it extracts the most salient statistical trends in data without the need for training sets. In this paper, we explore a large range of composite stellar population models defined for detailed analyses of galaxy spectra from surveys. Six of the most prominent spectral indices are targeted to visualize a PCA-based latent space created by the model data. The age-metallicity degeneracy is broken in the 3-dimensional space spanned by the first three eigenvectors, but we emphasize that non-trivial combinations of all six absorption indices are needed for this. Moreover, the last eigenvector suggests an intriguing tug of war between two Balmer indices: H$γ_A$ and $Hδ_A$, that can help discern the presence of recent bursting behaviour, as it exploits the different behaviour of the two indices over timescales $\sim$0.5-1 Gyr. Comparisons can be made between SDSS and LEGA-C galaxy spectra based on the latent space created by the models. This method, based on pure data, produces excellent results in agreement with standard SPS model fitting techniques, allowing for the study of stellar populations in a variety of surveys or observational/synthetic databases on solid ground.

AI.tldr: PCA applied to six spectral indices from composite stellar population models creates a latent space that breaks the age-metallicity degeneracy in 3D, with the fourth eigenvector revealing a HγA-HδA balance sensitive to recent bursting behavior. The method aligns with standard SPS fitting and enables cross-survey comparisons (SDSS & LEGA-C).
AI.motivation: To provide a simple, interpretable, non-parametric alternative (PCA) to complex ML methods for analyzing galaxy spectra, specifically targeting the age-metallicity degeneracy and recent star formation history.
AI.method: PCA applied to six prominent spectral indices (including HγA, HδA) from a large grid of composite stellar population models, creating a latent space where eigenvectors are analyzed; validation against SDSS and LEGA-C survey data.
AI.result: Age-metallicity degeneracy is broken in the 3D space of the first three PCs; the fourth eigenvector reveals a tension between HγA and HδA that traces bursting behavior over ~0.5-1 Gyr timescales; PCA results agree with standard SPS fitting.
AI.conclusion: PCA-based latent space using spectral indices is a robust, data-driven method for studying stellar populations across different surveys, providing interpretable results consistent with traditional SPS techniques.

title: Multi-line Wave Signatures in a Sunspot from Near-UV Sunrise III/SUSI Observations
comment: Accepted for publication in The Astrophysical Journal Letters
summary: Magnetohydrodynamic waves redistribute energy in magnetic structures of the lower solar atmosphere, yet constraints on how wave power and dominant frequencies are organised above sunspots remain limited because most studies use only a few well-separated diagnostics. Here we present multiline wave signatures in a sunspot from near-UV spectroscopy with the Sunrise-III UV Spectropolarimeter and Imager (SUSI). We analyse a two-hour time series of repeated raster scans of a sunspot near disc centre in the 327-329 nm spectral window (> 100 lines). From these, we select 44 lines that radiative-transfer calculations suggest sample effective formation heights within the umbral core from deep photosphere toward the low chromosphere. For each line, we extract line-core intensity and line-of-sight velocity time series using a dedicated multi-line fitting routine and compute Morlet-wavelet power spectra. The refined global wavelet spectra show that most lines (in both intensity and velocity) are genuinely multi-frequency, with a dominant peak and substantial statistically significant power up to 12 mHz. Unsupervised clustering of the normalised spectra groups lines into families with similar spectral shapes and reveals a progression of dominant frequencies from ~2 to ~10 mHz across the ensemble, for both intensity and velocity (not necessarily in the same lines). This behaviour is not reproduced by a simple formation-height ranking, suggesting that uncertainties in the formation-height estimates and line-dependent diagnostic response together shape the ordering. These Sunrise-III/SUSI observations open a new regime for near-UV multi-line wave studies and provide the first systematic characterisation of frequency-structured sunspot wave behaviour in this spectral region.

AI.tldr: This paper presents multiline wave signatures in a sunspot using near-UV spectroscopy from Sunrise-III/SUSI, analyzing 44 spectral lines from 327-329 nm. Global wavelet spectra reveal multi-frequency behavior with dominant peaks up to 12 mHz. Unsupervised clustering groups lines into families with distinct frequency progressions (~2-10 mHz), showing that wave power organization is not simply explained by formation height rankings.
AI.motivation: Constraints on how wave power and dominant frequencies are organized above sunspots remain limited because most studies use only a few well-separated diagnostics.
AI.method: Two-hour time series of repeated raster scans of a sunspot near disc centre in the 327-329 nm spectral window (>100 lines). 44 lines selected based on radiative-transfer calculations. Line-core intensity and LOS velocity extracted via dedicated multi-line fitting. Morlet-wavelet power spectra computed. Unsupervised clustering applied to normalized spectra.
AI.result: Most lines show multi-frequency behavior with statistically significant power up to 12 mHz. Clustering reveals families with similar spectral shapes and a progression of dominant frequencies from ~2 to ~10 mHz. This ordering is not reproduced by simple formation-height ranking.
AI.conclusion: Sunrise-III/SUSI opens a new regime for near-UV multi-line wave studies and provides the first systematic characterization of frequency-structured sunspot wave behavior in this spectral region.

title: GA-NIFS: The interplay between feedback and star formation at 3 < z < 9 probed by JWST/NIRSpec IFU
comment: 23 pages, 25 figures, submitted to A&A
summary: The study of starburst- and AGN-driven feedback is fundamental for understanding the processes that shape galaxy growth, quench star formation, and drive the co-evolution of galaxies and their central black holes. We present a spatially resolved study of six galaxies at $3 < z < 9$, including starburst- and AGN-dominated systems, observed with JWST/NIRSpec IFU in low- ($R \sim 100$) and high-resolution ($R \sim 2700$) mode. Previous analysis of $R \sim 2700$ data revealed ionized outflows in all these galaxies. We explore possible links between outflows and stellar population properties to assess the mechanisms driving galaxy evolution at early epochs. Combining the spatially resolved stellar population analysis with the outflow properties, we find that the most massive galaxies ($M_\star > 5 \times 10^{10} M_\odot$) with strong AGN-driven ionized outflows show evidence of past quenching episodes occurring within the last $\sim 100$--$300$ Myr, mainly in the nuclear regions ($r < 3$ kpc). In contrast, higher-redshift ($z > 5$) and less massive ($M_\star < 10^{10} M_\odot$) starburst galaxies with powerful (starburst-driven) outflows appear to have experienced continuous growth, with no clear sign of quenching. Massive galaxies with weaker outflows do not show evidence of quenching in their history. One massive AGN host (GS20936) shows evidence for a recent ($10$--$30$ Myr) rejuvenation phase, likely fueled by a recent major merger. These results suggest that (AGN-driven) outflows can already play a key role in shaping the SFHs of massive galaxies at early cosmic epochs.

AI.tldr: JWST/NIRSpec IFU study of 6 z~3-9 galaxies reveals that massive galaxies with strong AGN-driven outflows show past quenching (100-300 Myr ago) in nuclear regions, while lower-mass starburst galaxies with powerful outflows show continuous growth without quenching, suggesting AGN-driven outflows already shape massive galaxy evolution at early epochs.
AI.motivation: To understand starburst- and AGN-driven feedback mechanisms that shape galaxy growth, quench star formation, and drive co-evolution of galaxies and their central black holes at early cosmic epochs.
AI.method: Spatially resolved study of 6 galaxies at 3<z<9 using JWST/NIRSpec IFU in low (R~100) and high-resolution (R~2700) mode, combining spatially resolved stellar population analysis with outflow properties.
AI.result: Massive galaxies (M_*>5e10 M_sun) with strong AGN-driven outflows show past quenching within last ~100-300 Myr in nuclear regions (r<3 kpc); higher-redshift (z>5) less massive starburst galaxies with powerful outflows show continuous growth; one massive AGN host shows recent rejuvenation (10-30 Myr) likely from a major merger.
AI.conclusion: AGN-driven outflows can already play a key role in shaping star formation histories of massive galaxies at early cosmic epochs.

title: Magnetically Structured Oscillatory Power Along an Active-Region Transect in Near-UV Sunrise-III/SUSI Spectroscopy
comment: Accepted for publication in The Astrophysical Journal Letters
summary: We present a multi-line characterisation of how oscillatory power is organised across distinct magnetic environments in an active region using seeing-free, stratospheric near-ultraviolet spectroscopy from the Sunrise-III UV Spectropolarimeter and Imager (SUSI). A two-hour time series of short raster scans in the line-rich 327-329 nm window samples along a single transect that contains the following regions: weak magnetic-field surroundings, a plage, a sunspot, and a pore. From a set of 30 selected, relatively unblended absorption lines, we extract line-core Doppler-velocity time series and compute Morlet-wavelet refined global spectra from which we form band-integrated power maps for three frequency bands (2-4, 4-6, and 6-12 mHz). The stacked, line-resolved maps reveal a clear environment-dependent redistribution of power: 2-4 mHz power is strongest in the weak-field/plage segments but is commonly suppressed in the umbra and pore cores, while 4-6 mHz and 6-12 mHz power becomes relatively enhanced in the strongest-field regions, with line-dependent behaviour in the penumbra and plage. Across the line ensemble, this broad frequency structuring is coherent, but the detailed spatial distribution and relative band ranking are not identical from line to line - even among spectral lines with comparable effective formation depths - demonstrating clear line dependence. This novel result implies that single-line measurements may miss secondary components of the local wave spectrum because different lines weight co-existing perturbations and modes differently; therefore, the SUSI near-UV window provides a uniquely diagnostic-rich mapping of oscillations, offering leverage that is difficult to obtain with traditional one- or two-line approaches.

AI.tldr: Using Sunrise-III SUSI stratospheric near-UV spectroscopy (327-329 nm), the authors analyze a two-hour time series of 30 absorption lines across distinct magnetic environments (weak-field, plage, sunspot, pore) in an active region. They produce band-integrated power maps (2-4, 4-6, 6-12 mHz) that show environment-dependent redistribution of oscillatory power, with clear line-dependent behaviour even among lines with similar formation depths. This demonstrates that single-line measurements miss secondary wave-spectrum components, and the SUSI near-UV window offers uniquely diagnostic-rich multi-line oscillation mapping.
AI.motivation: To understand how oscillatory power is organized across different magnetic environments in an active region, and to demonstrate that multi-line spectroscopy in the near-UV reveals wave-spectrum components that single-line approaches cannot capture.
AI.method: Seeing-free stratospheric near-UV spectroscopy from Sunrise-III SUSI; two-hour time series of short raster scans in the 327-329 nm window; 30 selected absorption lines; Morlet-wavelet refined global spectra; band-integrated power maps for 2-4, 4-6, 6-12 mHz bands; stacked line-resolved mapping across weak-field, plage, sunspot, and pore regions.
AI.result: 2-4 mHz power is strongest in weak-field/plage but suppressed in umbra/pore cores; 4-6 mHz and 6-12 mHz power is enhanced in strongest-field regions; spatial distribution and band ranking vary from line to line even at comparable formation depths, showing clear line dependence.
AI.conclusion: Multi-line near-UV spectroscopy reveals that single-line measurements miss secondary components of the local wave spectrum because different lines weight co-existing perturbations differently. The SUSI near-UV window provides uniquely diagnostic-rich oscillation mapping unattainable with traditional one- or two-line approaches.

title: The S-PLUS Fornax Project (S+FP): Fornax-like clusters in cosmological hydrodynamical simulations
comment: 15 pages, 6 figures. Accepted for publication in A&A
summary: The Fornax galaxy cluster constitutes a suitable laboratory to explore the evolution of galaxies in a dense environment. Recently, the Southern Photometric Local Universe Survey (S-PLUS) has obtained unprecedented photometric information of Fornax, revealing new features regarding its galaxy populations and surrounding regions. In this context, simulations are invaluable tools to interpret the past, present and fate of such observational findings. We aim to deliver a robust photometric catalog of simulated Fornax-like systems in cosmological context, to consistently contrast them with S-PLUS data. We analyze Fornax analogs from the EAGLE and IllustrisTNG simulations, selected using observed properties of the Fornax cluster and its central galaxy NGC 1399. For each system, we generated synthetic photometry in the 12 S-PLUS bands using the SKIRT radiative transfer code, reproducing the instrumental configuration of the S-PLUS survey. Simulated data cubes, mock images, spectral energy distributions, magnitudes and colors were obtained for each galaxy in our selected simulated Fornax analogs. The synthetic photometry and spectra derived from simulations show a good agreement with the S-PLUS observations. We identify particular systems which show some similarity with the spatial distribution of galaxies in Fornax. Such simulated candidates reproduce the observed color-magnitude relation and the spatial substructure between the cluster core and the Fornax A region. Also, simulated galaxies are bluer at higher cluster-centric distances, in agreement with observations. Although modest discrepancies were obtained between the observed and simulated color-magnitude diagrams in some cases, our results support the suitability of our selection criteria and synthetic photometry, and the reliability of current cosmological simulations to reproduce key general features of the Fornax cluster.

AI.tldr: The authors created synthetic photometric catalogs of simulated Fornax-like galaxy clusters using EAGLE and IllustrisTNG, processed through SKIRT radiative transfer to match S-PLUS observations, finding good agreement in color-magnitude relations, spatial substructures, and radial color gradients.
AI.motivation: To deliver a robust photometric catalog of simulated Fornax-like systems in cosmological context to consistently contrast them with S-PLUS observational data, enabling interpretation of galaxy evolution in dense environments.
AI.method: Fornax analogs were selected from EAGLE and IllustrisTNG simulations using observed properties of the Fornax cluster and NGC 1399. Synthetic photometry in 12 S-PLUS bands was generated using the SKIRT radiative transfer code, reproducing the instrumental configuration of the S-PLUS survey. Simulated data cubes, mock images, SEDs, magnitudes, and colors were produced for each galaxy.
AI.result: Synthetic photometry and spectra show good agreement with S-PLUS observations. Selected simulated candidates reproduce the observed color-magnitude relation and spatial substructure between the cluster core and Fornax A region. Simulated galaxies are bluer at higher cluster-centric distances, matching observations. Some modest discrepancies in color-magnitude diagrams were noted.
AI.conclusion: The selection criteria and synthetic photometry approach are suitable, and current cosmological simulations (EAGLE, IllustrisTNG) reliably reproduce key general features of the Fornax cluster.

title: Characterization of white-light enhancements under umbral conditions in one-dimensional simulations of solar flares
comment: Abstract shortened for Arxiv
summary: Solar flares with signatures in the optical continuum (white light, WL) pose a challenge to the standard flare model and to solar flare simulations. In particular, simulations are so far not able to convincingly reproduce observed WL enhancements. We investigate the effect of different electron beams on an umbral atmosphere and what the differences and similarities to the quiet-Sun response are. We characterized WL emission in one-dimensional simulations of solar flares using the radiation hydrodynamics code RADYN. We used a similar setup as the F-CHROMA grid, but with a starting atmosphere describing umbral conditions. We investigated the influence of different temporal profiles of an electron beam on this umbral atmosphere. Our simulations show maximum WL increases between 40 and 335%, which is comparable to observed values. The reduced umbral background is the main reason for these large increases. We identify hydrogen recombination in an optically thin chromosphere as the dominant process responsible for the increases, with the radiation from the heated photosphere becoming substantial in the later stages due to the longer timescale of the cooling of the photosphere compared to hydrogen recombination in the chromosphere. Shorter, more intense beams (i.e., beams with a higher maximum energy flux) lead to a faster and more dramatic atmospheric evolution. Such beams also cause larger WL enhancements due to a higher electron density in the relevant layers. Both the Balmer ratio and the Paschen ratio are substantially higher in our simulations compared to simulations with a quiet-Sun atmosphere. The detectability and amplitude of WL enhancements depends on the spectral and temporal structure of the electron beam as well as the underlying background radiation. The combination of a short, intense beam and an umbral atmosphere provides an excellent seed for substantial WL enhancements.

AI.tldr: This paper uses 1D RADYN simulations to study white-light (WL) emission from electron beams in umbral atmospheres, finding WL enhancements of 40–335%—much larger than in quiet-Sun simulations—driven primarily by hydrogen recombination in an optically thin chromosphere, with shorter, more intense beams producing larger enhancements due to higher electron density.
AI.motivation: Solar flares with white-light (optical continuum) signatures challenge the standard flare model and existing simulations, which fail to convincingly reproduce observed WL enhancements.
AI.method: 1D radiation hydrodynamics simulations using the RADYN code, with an umbral starting atmosphere and varied temporal electron beam profiles, similar to the F-CHROMA grid setup.
AI.result: Simulated WL increases of 40–335%, comparable to observations; hydrogen recombination in an optically thin chromosphere is the dominant mechanism, with photospheric heating contributing later. Shorter, more intense beams yield faster evolution and larger WL enhancements due to higher electron density.
AI.conclusion: The combination of a short, intense electron beam and an umbral atmosphere is particularly effective for producing substantial WL enhancements; detectability and amplitude depend on beam spectral/temporal structure and background radiation.

title: Identifying Warped Galaxies in Pan-STARRS and Euclid using Deep Convolutional Neural Network
comment: 14 pages, 14 Figures, 3 tables (Submitted)
summary: Warped galactic discs are common, yet their detection remains challenging, as the outskirts of galaxies are typically faint. Advances in deep imaging surveys improve the detectability of such features, while machine learning enables efficient analysis of large datasets. Using the Pan-STARRS EGIPS catalogue, we develop a deep learning framework by fine-tuning the Zoobot convNext-nano model on 1000 edge-on galaxy FITS images to distinguish warped and non-warped edge-on galaxies with 83\% accuracy. The trained model is then applied to a larger sample, identifying 2088 warped and 1398 non-warped galaxies with a high prediction probability threshold ($\geq 0.85$). Additionally, we use the model to predict on 3226 edge-on galaxies from the Euclid Q1 survey, demonstrating the model's ability to generalise across datasets with differing resolutions. To analyse the model predictions, we employ LayerCAM to identify the regions of galaxy images that contribute to the classification. We find that warped galaxies differ primarily in their structural properties, exhibiting lower axis ratios and higher asymmetry. Warped galaxies were found to be bluer, with younger stellar populations and enhanced star formation. These results highlight the effectiveness of deep learning methods in identifying subtle morphological features, such as warps, and demonstrate their potential for studying structural properties of galaxies in current and upcoming large imaging surveys.

AI.tldr: A deep learning framework (fine-tuned Zoobot convNext-nano) classifies warped vs. non-warped edge-on galaxies with 83% accuracy using Pan-STARRS data, identifies 2088 warped galaxies, generalizes to Euclid Q1 data, and reveals warped galaxies have lower axis ratios, higher asymmetry, bluer colors, younger stellar populations, and enhanced star formation.
AI.motivation: Warped galactic discs are common but difficult to detect due to faint galaxy outskirts; deep imaging surveys and machine learning offer a path to efficiently identify these subtle morphological features in large datasets.
AI.method: Fine-tuned the Zoobot convNext-nano model on 1000 edge-on galaxy FITS images from the Pan-STARRS EGIPS catalogue to classify warped vs. non-warped galaxies; applied the trained model to a larger sample and to Euclid Q1 survey data; used LayerCAM for interpretability and analyzed structural and photometric properties.
AI.result: Achieved 83% classification accuracy; identified 2088 warped and 1398 non-warped galaxies at ≥0.85 prediction probability; the model generalized to Euclid Q1 data; warped galaxies exhibit lower axis ratios, higher asymmetry, bluer colors, younger stellar populations, and enhanced star formation.
AI.conclusion: Deep learning methods are effective at identifying subtle morphological features like warps and show strong potential for studying galaxy structural properties in current and upcoming large imaging surveys.

title: Gravity-mode main-sequence pulsators in the open clusters NGC 3532 and NGC 2516: Instability strip, near-core rotation, and internal structure
comment: Main text: 15 pages, 12 figures, and 2 tables. Appendices: 11 pages, 14 figures, and 8 tables. Accepted for publication in A&A. Due to the character limit, the abstract in the arXiv version is shorter than the abstract in the main text
summary: Context. Studying pulsating stars in clusters opens a new window onto stellar physics. Gravity-mode (g-mode) pulsators in open clusters allow us to measure their near-core rotation rates and, together with cluster age and mass constraints, test angular momentum transport in stars above about 1.5 solar masses. Aims. We aim to detect g-mode pulsations in member stars of the young open cluster NGC 3532, about 300 Myr old, and to measure their near-core rotation rates and internal properties. Methods. We used TESS photometry to extract light curves of NGC 3532 members. The observed g-mode period spacings allow us to measure near-core rotation rates and the asymptotic period spacing, Pi0. We also fitted isochrones to the colour-magnitude diagrams of NGC 3532 and NGC 2516 to refine the cluster ages and obtain stellar masses. Results. We constrain the observed instability region of young gamma Doradus members from a blue edge at about 7760 K to a red edge at about 7070 K, while some hotter g-mode pulsators are also seen. The near-core rotation rates show a rotation-mass relation similar to that in NGC 2516: below 1.6 solar masses, the rotation rate increases with mass, whereas above 1.6 solar masses the NGC 3532 stars reach a plateau at about 2.8 d^-1. This mass may mark a threshold between different rotational spin-down mechanisms. Existing evolutionary models with angular momentum transport imply that these g-mode pulsators were born rotating above 55 percent of the critical value. Our simplified models, assuming spherical symmetry, angular momentum conservation, and rigid internal rotation, suggest that either mass-dependent initial rotation rates are required, or that minor angular momentum loss still operates above 1.6 solar masses. Finally, our Pi0 measurements reveal a discrepancy with theoretical predictions for some pulsators, as also found in the younger cluster NGC 2516.

AI.tldr: Using TESS photometry, this paper studies g-mode pulsations in gamma Doradus stars of the young open cluster NGC 3532 (~300 Myr). Near-core rotation rates show a mass-dependent trend: increasing below 1.6 solar masses and plateauing at ~2.8 d⁻¹ above it, suggesting a threshold between different spin-down mechanisms. Discrepancies between observed asymptotic period spacings (Pi0) and theoretical predictions are noted.
AI.motivation: To use g-mode pulsators in open clusters to measure near-core rotation rates and, combined with cluster age and mass constraints, test angular momentum transport in stars above ~1.5 solar masses.
AI.method: TESS photometry for light curves of NGC 3532 members; measurement of g-mode period spacings to infer near-core rotation rates and asymptotic period spacing (Pi0); isochrone fitting to colour-magnitude diagrams of NGC 3532 and NGC 2516 for age and mass refinement.
AI.result: Instability region of gamma Doradus members constrained between ~7760 K (blue edge) and ~7070 K (red edge). Near-core rotation rates show a rotation-mass relation: increasing with mass below 1.6 M☉, plateauing at ~2.8 d⁻¹ above it. This mass may separate different spin-down regimes. Pi0 measurements show discrepancies with theory, similar to NGC 2516.
AI.conclusion: The 1.6 M☉ threshold likely marks a transition between rotational spin-down mechanisms. Existing evolutionary models imply these stars were born rotating >55% of critical. Simplified models suggest either mass-dependent initial rotation or continued minor angular momentum loss above 1.6 M☉. Pi0 discrepancies require further theoretical investigation.

title: Uncovering DM distribution by combining stellar kinematics and integrated HI spectra: method validation
comment: 23 pages, 18 figures; submitted to Astronomy & Astrophysics
summary: We determine the dark matter (DM) distribution in galaxies by jointly modelling stellar kinematics from IFU observations and the gaseous kinematics encoded in a single integrated HI spectrum. The stellar kinematics are described by a triaxial orbit-superposition Schwarzschild model, while the HI gas is described by an idealised disc model; both are governed by the same gravitational potential. The potential comprises the stellar mass, a generalised NFW DM halo, and a central black hole. We validate the method on 58 simulated galaxies generated from the TNG50 cosmological simulation. For each galaxy, we create two versions of mock data with azimuthal angles viewed side-on and end-on thus 116 mock observations in total. Our model recovers the total mass, stellar mass, and DM mass profiles within the data range; the median DM mass of the 58 simulated galaxies is recovered with a relative systematic bias smaller than 20% across all radii from 2--20 kpc. The statistical uncertainties on the DM masses within 5 kpc remain similar to those found with the model constrained by IFU data only. In contrast, the relative uncertainty on the DM mass in the outer regions decreases once the HI spectrum is included; at 20 kpc, it drops markedly, from about 85% to roughly 30%. The DM density slope defined explicitly in the gNFW model is systematically underestimated and thus does not yield a reliable quantity from observations using our approach. Instead, we introduce density slopes evaluated between 2 and 20 kpc, which are statistically well recovered for both the total mass and the DM mass. We demonstrate the reliability of this method in uncovering DM distribution and emphasize its promise for application to large samples of observed galaxies.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a method that jointly models stellar kinematics (from IFU) and HI gas kinematics to determine dark matter distribution in galaxies. Validated on 58 simulated TNG50 galaxies (116 mock observations), it recovers mass profiles with <20% systematic bias in DM mass across 2–20 kpc, and reduces outer-region DM uncertainty from ~85% to ~30% at 20 kpc by adding HI data.
AI.motivation: To improve constraints on dark matter distribution in galaxies, especially in the outer regions, by combining stellar IFU kinematics with integrated HI gas kinematics, overcoming limitations of using stellar kinematics alone.
AI.method: Jointly model stellar kinematics (triaxial orbit-superposition Schwarzschild model) and HI gas kinematics (idealised disc model) under a common gravitational potential (stellar mass + gNFW DM halo + central BH). Validated on 58 TNG50 simulated galaxies with side-on and end-on mock observations (116 total).
AI.result: Total, stellar, and DM mass profiles recovered within data range; median DM mass bias <20% across 2–20 kpc. Adding HI data keeps inner (5 kpc) DM uncertainty similar to IFU-only but reduces outer (20 kpc) uncertainty from ~85% to ~30%. The gNFW DM slope is systematically underestimated; slope evaluated between 2–20 kpc is reliably recovered.
AI.conclusion: The joint modelling approach reliably uncovers DM distribution, particularly in outer galaxy regions, and is promising for application to large galaxy samples.

title: Morphokinematic structure of the Planetary Nebula NGC 6563
comment: 17 pages, 7 figures, published in the journal Galaxies (https://www.mdpi.com/2075-4434/14/3/60)
summary: We present a morphokinematic analysis based on high-resolution long-slit echelle spectroscopy of the \nii$\lambda6583$ line and narrowband imaging. Position-velocity diagrams reveal asymmetric expansion and localized kinematic features. We derive a systemic velocity of $V_{\rm sys}^{\rm LSR} = -25\pm1$\kms\ ($V_{\rm sys}^{\rm HEL} = -34 \pm 1$\kms) and a main shell expansion velocity of $V_{\rm exp} = 22 \pm 1$\kms. Three-dimensional modeling indicates an ellipsoidal main body surrounded by a thin shell, two ear-like protrusions, and additional small-scale structures. The corresponding kinematic ages are $3\,600 \pm 700$ yr for the ellipsoid and ring, and $7\,500 \pm 1\,000$ yr and $8\,800 \pm 1\,500$ yr for the two opposite ear-like protrusions, respectively, indicating that these outer structures predate the main nebular envelope. The kinematic asymmetry and enhanced emission regions suggest evolution within a non-uniform ambient medium. At the same time, the presence of collimated ear-like structures is consistent with shaping influenced by binary interaction, where earlier outflows preceded the ejection of the dense shell. NGC\,6563 therefore appears to be a dynamically evolved system shaped by the combined effects of episodic mass ejection and environmental interaction.

AI.tldr: Morphokinematic analysis of NGC 6563 reveals asymmetric expansion, a main shell expansion velocity of 22 km/s, and ear-like protrusions predating the main nebular envelope, suggesting episodic mass ejection and binary interaction in a non-uniform ambient medium.
AI.motivation: To understand the kinematic structure, formation history, and shaping mechanisms of the planetary nebula NGC 6563 through high-resolution spectroscopy and 3D modeling.
AI.method: High-resolution long-slit echelle spectroscopy of the [N II] λ6583 line, narrowband imaging, position-velocity diagrams, and three-dimensional morphological-kinematic modeling.
AI.result: Systemic velocity Vsys^LSR = -25±1 km/s; expansion velocity Vexp = 22±1 km/s. Kinematic ages: ellipsoid/ring ~3,600±700 yr; ear-like protrusions ~7,500±1,000 yr and 8,800±1,500 yr. Ellipsoidal main body with thin shell, two ear-like protrusions, and small-scale structures.
AI.conclusion: NGC 6563 is a dynamically evolved planetary nebula shaped by episodic mass ejection and binary interaction, evolving within a non-uniform ambient medium; the outer ear-like structures predate the main nebular envelope.

title: Lensed hot stars with HST in the 2030s
comment: 6 pages, 3 figures; white paper submitted in response to the Space Telescope Science Institute call: Building a Roadmap for Hubble science into the 2030s
summary: In the late 20th century, the Hubble Space Telescope (HST) revolutionized astronomy, showing the Universe with a detail never seen before in the ultraviolet (UV), optical and infrared (IR) bands. In the early 2020s, the James Webb Space Telescope started a similar revolution in the IR. The launch of Roman in late 2026 challenges the reign of HST in the optical band, but even after Roman's launch, HST will remain as the only telescope capable of high-quality imaging in the UV band. In the optical bands, HST provides superior resolution than Roman for point sources. Although equipped with more sensitive MOS, Roman's sensors have a pixel size about 3 times larger than HST's CCDs, hence undersampling the point-spread-function, and resulting in a worse spatial resolution. The UV-capable and higher-resolution of HST in the UV and optical band, makes HST the best instrument for specific science cases. This paper responds to the "Building a Roadmap for Hubble science into the 2030s" call and focuses on science with lensed hot stars at $z>0.5$ in the UV and optical bands, exploiting the features that makes HST the best instrument in the UV/optical until the launch of the Habitable World Observatory in the 2040s.

AI.tldr: This paper argues that despite upcoming telescopes like Roman, HST will remain uniquely valuable for UV/optical science, particularly for studying lensed hot stars at z>0.5, due to its superior UV capability and higher spatial resolution in optical bands.
AI.motivation: To respond to the "Building a Roadmap for Hubble science into the 2030s" call by identifying niche science cases where HST remains irreplaceable after Roman's launch, specifically focusing on UV and optical observations of lensed hot stars at high redshift.
AI.method: The paper compares the capabilities of HST, Roman, and JWST across UV, optical, and IR bands, highlighting HST's unique advantages: sole high-quality UV imaging capability, superior optical resolution for point sources (due to Roman's larger pixels causing undersampling), and the synergy of these features for targeted science cases.
AI.result: HST will remain the only telescope capable of high-quality UV imaging after Roman's launch, and provides better optical spatial resolution for point sources than Roman. These unique capabilities make HST the best instrument for specific science cases, such as studying lensed hot stars at z>0.5, until the Habitable World Observatory launches in the 2040s.
AI.conclusion: HST continues to be essential for UV and high-resolution optical astronomy into the 2030s, complementing Roman and JWST, and should be prioritized for niche science like lensed hot stars at high redshift that cannot be done with other facilities.

title: Operational forecasting of solar energetic particle event and proton flux using multi-source solar observations and multi-task deep learning
summary: Solar energetic particle (SEP) events, defined by proton flux exceeding 10 pfu in the $>$ 10 MeV channel, pose major risks to spacecraft operations, astronaut safety, and high-latitude aviation. Due to the complexity and rarity of SEP events, reliable operational SEP forecasting remains an important challenge in space weather. Here we present a novel 24-hour-ahead operational forecasting framework based on a multi-task learning structure with a thoroughly constructed list of features from multiple sources that span over multiple solar cycles. It extends an earlier-introduced \texttt{SEPNET}-based models by integrating a broader range of solar observations, including active region magnetic parameters from SHARP and SMARP, solar flares information, coronal mass ejections, soft X-ray flux, and historical $>$ 10 MeV proton flux. The inclusion of SMARP data expands the temporal coverage of magnetic-field predictors to earlier solar cycles, while flux-based inputs provide additional precursor information. Building on the multi-task architecture, we develop \texttt{SEPNET-Ov2}, which jointly predicts SEP event occurrence together with future proton flux and soft X-ray flux. Evaluation on the CLEAR SEP benchmark dataset shows improved classification performance over the earlier \texttt{SEPNET-O} (operational version of \texttt{SEPNET}) on the newly aligned dataset. The best operational model is obtained when magnetic, radiative, and proton-flux predictors are combined, highlighting the value of expanded historical coverage and complementary precursor information for improving operational SEP forecasting.

AI.tldr: The paper presents SEPNET-Ov2, a multi-task learning framework for 24-hour-ahead forecasting of solar energetic particle events. It integrates broader solar observations (SHARP, SMARP, flares, CMEs, X-ray/proton flux) and jointly predicts SEP occurrence, future proton flux, and soft X-ray flux. The model shows improved performance on the CLEAR SEP benchmark compared to its predecessor SEPNET-O.
AI.motivation: To improve operational SEP forecasting, which is crucial for spacecraft, astronaut, and aviation safety, by overcoming limitations of previous models through expanded historical data coverage and multi-source precursor information.
AI.method: Multi-task learning architecture (SEPNET-Ov2) jointly predicting SEP occurrence, future proton flux (>10 MeV), and soft X-ray flux. Features include SHARP/SMARP magnetic parameters, solar flare information, CME data, soft X-ray flux, and historical proton flux. SMARP extends magnetic-field predictors to earlier solar cycles.
AI.result: Outperformed earlier SEPNET-O model on the CLEAR SEP benchmark dataset. Best performance achieved when combining magnetic, radiative, and proton-flux predictors.
AI.conclusion: Expanded historical coverage (via SMARP) and complementary precursor information from multiple sources are valuable for improving operational SEP forecasting performance.

title: GATOS N: Extended circumnuclear dust emission in nearby Seyfert galaxies surveyed by JWST/MIRI
comment: 31 pages, 18 figures, submitted to MNRAS
summary: The subarcsecond angular resolution and stable background of JWST has given us the first high-fidelity images of the arcsecond-scale environment around Active Galactic Nuclei (AGNs) in the nearby Universe. With mid-infrared (MIR) surface brightness sensitivities that are much deeper than the best ground-based instruments, the Mid-InfraRed Instrument imager (MIRIM) now allows us to understand the structure and thermal properties of dust using information over wavelengths of $5$-$25$ $μ$m, almost all of the MIR range. We present a Cycle 1 JWST MIRIM survey of Seyfert galaxies with the express aim of characterising AGN-heated dust in the central few 100 pcs, and searching for signatures of dust-laden nuclear outflows. This paper outlines the motivation behind the programme, the data reduction and analysis techniques used to isolate the nuclear and extended emission, and a comparison of the observed MIR structures with those seen in other phases (stars, ionised and molecular gas, absorbing dust). In concert with earlier studies that used these data, we conclude that resolved AGN-heated dust is widespread in the Seyfert population, extending out to a few hundred pcs from the nucleus and often displaying a higher surface-brightness compared to the more widespread star-forming dusty circumnuclear disk. Even after accounting for contamination from emission lines in the MIRI filters, we find strong spatial correlations between MIR dust emission and the AGN-ionised gas in the narrow-line region (NLR).

AI.tldr: JWST MIRIM survey of Seyfert galaxies resolves AGN-heated dust on subarcsecond scales (few 100 pc), showing warm dust spatially correlated with ionized gas in the narrow-line region, extending beyond the star-forming circumnuclear disk.
AI.motivation: To characterize AGN-heated dust in the central few hundred parsecs of nearby Seyfert galaxies and search for signatures of dust-laden nuclear outflows using JWST's unprecedented MIR sensitivity and resolution.
AI.method: Cycle 1 JWST MIRIM survey (5–25 μm) of Seyfert galaxies; data reduction and analysis isolating nuclear vs. extended emission; comparison with multi-phase tracers (stars, ionized/molecular gas, dust absorption).
AI.result: Resolved AGN-heated dust is widespread in Seyferts, extending to a few 100 pc with higher surface brightness than the star-forming circumnuclear disk. Strong spatial correlation between MIR dust emission and NLR ionized gas, even after accounting for emission-line contamination.
AI.conclusion: JWST MIRI enables robust characterization of warm AGN-heated dust on arcsecond scales; the spatial correlation with NLR gas suggests a physical link between dust and AGN ionization cones/outflows.

title: A new CIGALE module for modeling AGN emission lines
summary:
Aims. The increasing discovery of high-redshift AGNs in recent years imposes more stringent requirements on spectral analysis tools for deriving the properties of AGNs and their host galaxies from emission-line diagnostics. To address this need, we develop a new module for the popular SED-fitting tool Code Investigating GALaxy Emission (CIGALE), the [nebular_AGN] module, which enables the efficient and flexible simulation and fitting of emission lines originating from the broad-line regions (BLRs) and narrow-line regions (NLRs) of AGNs, and allows the estimation of the physical properties of these regions.
  Methods. We use the spectral synthesis code Cloudy to construct the database for the new module. Based on the X-ray and accretion disk continua implemented in CIGALE, we generate the incident radiation fields of the models. We then adopt the AGN geometry and dust settings implemented in CIGALE to define a flexible set of physical parameters for the gas clouds, thereby producing a comprehensive database for the [nebular_AGN] module.
  Results. We benchmark the [nebular_AGN] module using a quasar composite spectrum, an empirical metallicity calibration, and observational data from X-ray-selected AGNs. Our module can approximately reproduce the majority of quasar emission-line profiles, cover the key emission-line ratios observed in AGN samples, and provide an assessment of their physical properties. For specific combinations of parameters, the metallicity derived by our module is consistent with the empirical formula. We further compare our models with other photoionization models used to simulate AGN NLR emission, and perform a line-sensitivity study to identify the most effective diagnostic lines for each parameter in our module. Finally, we confirm that the dust attenuation law plays an important role in SED fitting.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces the [nebular_AGN] module for CIGALE, which simulates and fits emission lines from AGN broad-line and narrow-line regions using Cloudy-based photoionization models, and demonstrates its performance against composite spectra, metallicity calibrations, and observational AGN data.
AI.motivation: The increasing discovery of high-redshift AGNs requires more robust spectral analysis tools for deriving AGN and host galaxy properties from emission-line diagnostics, motivating the development of a new dedicated module within the CIGALE framework.
AI.method: The module uses Cloudy spectral synthesis code to construct a database of emission-line models. It builds incident radiation fields from CIGALE's X-ray and accretion disk continua, and adopts CIGALE's AGN geometry and dust settings to define flexible physical parameters for gas clouds in the BLR and NLR.
AI.result: The module reproduces quasar emission-line profiles, covers key emission-line ratios observed in AGN samples, yields metallicities consistent with empirical calibrations, and shows good agreement when compared to other photoionization models. A line-sensitivity study identifies the most effective diagnostic lines for each parameter, and the dust attenuation law is confirmed to be important in SED fitting.
AI.conclusion: The [nebular_AGN] module provides an efficient, flexible tool for simulating and fitting AGN emission lines within CIGALE, enabling estimation of physical properties of BLRs and NLRs across a wide range of AGN observations.

title: Enigmatic Line Broadening During Solar Flares: Magnetic Field Broadening?
summary: The origin of the extreme broadening observed in chromospheric metal lines during solar and stellar flares, particularly Mg II h&k and Ca II H&K, remains poorly understood. These lines often display Lorentzian like wings whose widths exceed standard Stark broadening predictions by factors of approx. 30, with no known collisional mechanism capable of producing such enhancements. We posit that magnetic fields are responsible for this additional broadening due to the increase of magnetic activity during flares. A magnetic-field distribution of the form where P(B) goes as B^-3 reproduces the observed Mg II profile wings while leaving H I Balmer lines and optically thin transitions largely unaffected. To explain the broadening using magnetic fields, the high B tail can extend up to 10^6 G with extremely low probabilities where the filling factors are less than about 10^-6. We propose that observations of flares using spectropolarimetry can verify whether the anomalous broadening is from magnetic structures in flare ribbons.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes that extreme broadening in chromospheric metal lines during flares (Mg II, Ca II) is caused by magnetic fields with a P(B) ∝ B⁻³ distribution, requiring field strengths up to 10⁶ G at very low filling factors (∼10⁻⁶), rather than by collisional (Stark) broadening. Spectropolarimetry is suggested to test this hypothesis.
AI.motivation: The origin of the extreme Lorentzian-like wing broadening observed in chromospheric metal lines (Mg II h&k, Ca II H&K) during solar and stellar flares is poorly understood, as standard Stark broadening predictions fall short by factors of ∼30 and no known collisional mechanism can account for the enhancement.
AI.method: The authors propose a magnetic-field distribution model P(B) ∝ B⁻³, where the high-field tail extends up to 10⁶ G with extremely low filling factors (<10⁻⁶), and test its effect on line profiles, showing it reproduces observed Mg II wings without affecting H I Balmer lines or optically thin transitions.
AI.result: The B⁻³ magnetic field distribution reproduces the observed Mg II profile wings. The required high-B tail reaches ∼10⁶ G but occupies negligible area (filling factors <10⁻⁶). H I Balmer lines and optically thin transitions remain largely unaffected, consistent with observations.
AI.conclusion: Magnetic fields, not collisions, are likely responsible for the anomalous broadening. Spectropolarimetric observations of flares can verify whether the broadening originates from magnetic structures in flare ribbons.

title: From THESAN-ZOOM to JWST: Predicting ionizing photon escape and the rise of UV-bright reionization sources
comment: 18 pages, 11 figures, submitted to MNRAS
summary: Understanding the sources and evolution of cosmic reionization remains a central challenge in astrophysics, with the escape of ionizing Lyman-continuum (LyC) photons from early galaxies representing a major uncertainty. In this work, we use more than 35,000 galaxy realisations from the THESAN-ZOOM cosmological radiation-hydrodynamic simulations to identify indirect diagnostics of the LyC photon escape fraction ($f_\mathrm{esc}$) and the LyC photon escape rate ($\dot{N}_\mathrm{ion,esc}$) across the redshift range $z=3-16$. We train random forest regression models using these diagnostics to predict both quantities. We present four models: two trained with the full set of simulation-derived indicators to predict $f_\mathrm{esc}$ and $\dot{N}_\mathrm{ion,esc}$, and two restricted to observables accessible to JWST photometric surveys. We find the 10-to-100$\,$Myr star-formation rate ratio ($\mathrm{SFR}_{10} / \mathrm{SFR}_{100}$) and the gas-to-stellar mass ratio ($M_\mathrm{gas} / M_*$) to be the strongest diagnostics of $f_\mathrm{esc}$, suggesting a strong relationship between ionizing photon escape and gas clearing through bursty star formation. In contrast, rest-frame UV ($1500 \, Å$) absolute magnitude ($M_\mathrm{UV}$) dominates $\dot{N}_\mathrm{ion,esc}$ prediction. Motivated by the strong predictive power of $M_\mathrm{UV}$, we combine observed UV luminosity functions with derived $\dot{N}_\mathrm{ion,esc} - M_\mathrm{UV}$ relations to construct histories of reionization. These are consistent with observational constraints, avoiding the recently reported crisis in the ionizing photon budget. Our analysis suggests that the bulk of reionization occurred rapidly after $z \approx 8$, driven by UV-bright galaxies, with the $M_\mathrm{UV} < -17$ populations providing the dominant contribution.
